# Platform etiquette

Every venue has house norms, and company participation follows them more carefully
than an individual would, because a company account is read as a guest everywhere it
posts.

On professional networks, replies stay in the thread they answer. Quote-posting a
practitioner's question to the company's own feed converts a conversation into an
audience play, and the author experiences it as being farmed for content. If a
thread inspires standalone writing, the piece is written later, generalized, with
the author asked before any identifiable detail is used.

On community forums, the company account follows each forum's self-promotion rules
to the letter and then some: where a forum allows one link per post, the company
uses links only when the answer is incomplete without one. Forum reputation is
earned by answers that stand alone.

On high-velocity feeds, the company does not join pile-ons, does not reply to bait,
and does not use trending-topic hooks for unrelated content. The feed rewards speed;
the company's advantage is accuracy, and the etiquette is to arrive slightly later
with something checkable.

Everywhere, typos are corrected with visible edit notes where the platform supports
them, and a factual error is corrected in a reply to the original, never by silent
deletion. The account behaves as if every action is being screenshotted, because
eventually one is.
